body:
Not sure how much it matters given that for the webpack workflow seems to work just fine with deps instead of peer deps - https://github.com/pkozlowski-opensource/ng2-webpack-play. 

> We could file a bug against npm to have an option to install and save peer dependencies automatically.

I don't think you want to open that can of worms again - https://github.com/npm/npm/issues/6565

if you use  a seed or CLI then you will not be affected. it's only if you
start your project from scratch via npm init or npm install angular2 --save
that you will need to do more.

I think it's ok to make "starting from scratch" more difficult because we
don't expect many people to do that.

What is the revised install experience without cli? Might have a workaround or try to find one. Not everyone will go for the cli.

something like: npm install --save angular2 rxjs es6-shim zone.js

> What is the revised install experience without cli? Might have a
> workaround or try to find one. Not everyone will go for the cli.
>

> https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5560#issuecomment-161520827.

of course things might get tricky if angular2 requires versions of peer
dependencies that are older than the latest version

On Wed, Dec 2, 2015 at 11:28 PM Igor Minar iminar@google.com wrote:

> something like: npm install --save angular2 rxjs es6-shim zone.js
> 
> On Wed, Dec 2, 2015 at 9:25 PM Ward Bell notifications@github.com wrote:
> 
> > What is the revised install experience without cli? Might have a
> > workaround or try to find one. Not everyone will go for the cli.
> > 
> > —
> > Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> > https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5560#issuecomment-161520827.

Right the peer deps have to have narrow version range for now. That's the
penalty for living on the edge. But that's a good thing because people
won't be able to accidentally use angular with wrong dependencies.
On Thu, Dec 3, 2015 at 5:01 AM Pawel Kozlowski notifications@github.com
wrote:

> something like: npm install --save angular2 rxjs es6-shim zone.js
> 
> @IgorMinar https://github.com/IgorMinar I don't think it is that simple
> as we might have a situation where all the latest versions (ones resolved
> and installed by npm when no version is specified) might not work together.
> RxJS is the one that worries me the most here. I guess we are in the
> special period where several projects (zone, Rx, ng2) are moving very fast
> so probability of getting into troubles is higher. Unless we "lock" peer
> dependencies to a very narrow range.
> 
> I would vote for differing decision on deps vs. peerDeps till we've got
> bundling story figured out since we need to look into the entire experience
> with ng2.
> 
> —

> https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5560#issuecomment-161630536.
